review the pull request, report each defect it introduces with the file and line it sits on, and give a merge verdict
---
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:459 — research-end fails every successful research ticket: the PostToolUse:Write hook (write-mutation-logger.sh) appends to .run/audit.jsonl when the subagent writes its report, and any file under .run/ newer than the dispatch marker is reported as the subagent changing files outside grimoires/loa/research/ (reproduced; .beads/ is hit the same way by any br call during a batch)
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:651 — the FR-1.1 spike carve-out fails open: `yq ... | jq -e` exits 0 when yq fails and prints nothing (jq 1.6 exits 0 on empty input; the hook has no pipefail), so an unparsable ledger lets `git branch -D spike/<slug>` with unmerged commits through; the PR's own test "an unparsable ledger keeps the block" fails on jq 1.6
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:159 — op_epic (and op_ticket:199, op_resolve:291, op_rule_out:331, op_handoff:351, op_research_begin:438) never check the unattended context; with LOA_UNATTENDED=1 chart-guard.sh refuses but chart-ticket.sh epic/ticket create the epic, the doc, open ledger rows and beads, so the interactive-only rule is prose-only
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:402 — close --consumed-by is allowed unattended on any map: on a charting map with open rows it rejects every row (line 414), closes every bead and the epic and marks the doc closed (reproduced); it should require Status handed-off and zero open rows; tests/unit/charting-decisions.bats:347 (CD-22) asserts the defective behaviour
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:830 — SP-1 does not inspect push refspecs: `git push origin spike/x:main` and `git push origin spike/x:refs/heads/feat` are allowed (verified), landing spike content on another branch with no merge or PR, and this hole is not in the documented Misses (:834-836); `git branch feat spike/x`, `git fetch origin spike/x:feat` and `git read-tree spike/x` are also allowed and undocumented
head/.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh:57 — the probe's only check is a before/after `git status` diff (lines 57-72); a probe that writes .git/hooks/*, sets core.hooksPath or moves refs in the main tree passes with exit 0 and runs later in the session, and the probe inherits the session's credentials/SSH agent; with SKILL.md:5 granting `Bash(.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh *)` under deny_raw_shell: true and no operator confirmation of the argv (SKILL.md:119-120), an untrusted research report is a direct path to arbitrary execution
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:127 — section_append passes free text to awk via -v, which expands backslash escapes; `--line 'x\n## Execution override\n...'` passes san1 and injects a new H2 into the tracked map doc (reproduced); set_status (:120) and section_bullets (:137) have the same pattern; use ENVIRON
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:172 — op_epic runs `br create` before writing the doc (mkdir/mktemp at :175); a doc write failure leaves an orphan map epic and the re-run creates a second one (reproduced: bd-map-m-1 and bd-map-m-2), contradicting the header's re-run-creates-only-what-is-missing claim
head/.claude/commands/chart.md:22 — grimoires/loa/research/chart-*.md (untrusted research reports, per SKILL.md Rules) are loaded raw as command context_files at /chart start, outside the L6 fence used at hand-off
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:304 — --answer-ref is optional on resolve and dec-write-lib drops it unattended; op_handoff (:351) then publishes proposed rows with no decided_by_ref as "settled; confirm, do not re-ask" priority-1 PRD context
head/.claude/scripts/run-mode-ice.sh:58 — the spike rule says a spike is never merged into another branch, but safe_push never parses `src:dst`; `run-mode-ice.sh push origin spike/x:master` pushed the spike commit onto master (exit 0); split the refspec and check the destination against protected patterns and the source against is_spike_branch (root cause predates the PR; the invariant it defeats is new)
head/.claude/commands/chart.md:57 — a new truename command and skill with no CHANGELOG entry and no CLAUDE.loa.md row for /chart or the charting phase (README/AGENTS counts were updated); Documentation Verification is blocking for approval
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:144 — map_rows globs a2a/*/decisions-pending.yaml relative to SCRIPT_DIR rather than --root/$G, so under --root it reads the live repo's pending files
head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:461 — `find -newer` has one-second granularity; a write in the marker's own second is not detected (CD-24 needs `sleep 1` to pass)
head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:1026 — the map validator's slug grammar (^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$) is wider than golden-path.sh:70 and chart-ticket.sh:44 (^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,47}$); a map doc such as Eval_Workers.md validates but is invisible to phase detection and the multi-map rule
head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:860 — _sp1_checkout_copies blocks `git checkout spike/notes.md other.md` (two paths under a spike/ directory, no ref), a false positive corpus row B57 already acknowledges as a non-ref
head/tests/unit/charting-decisions.bats:224 — CD-14 relies on `chmod a-w` to make the ledger write fail; running as root (common in CI containers) the write succeeds and the test fails for the wrong reason
head/.loa.config.yaml.example:443 — interview.unattended_prototype is documented with defer|halt semantics but nothing in the change reads the key; the behaviour is skill prose only (tests/unit/unattended-prototype.bats:6-8), so document it as advisory or wire it
head/.claude/agents/chart-researcher.md:5 — the researcher is given an unrestricted Write tool (and write_capable: true in agent-types.yaml:27) with "write exactly one file" enforced only by prose and the after-the-fact scope check of the first finding; returning the report as the final message and letting the session save it removes the write capability and the false failure
Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

# Audit Sprint

## Purpose

Security and quality audit of sprint implementation as the Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor. Final gate before sprint completion. Runs AFTER senior lead approval.

## Invocation

```
/audit-sprint sprint-1
/audit-sprint sprint-1 background
```

## Agent

Launches `auditing-security` from `skills/auditing-security/`.

See: `skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md` for full workflow details.

## Prerequisites

- Sprint tasks implemented (`/implement`)
- Senior lead approved with "All good" (`/review-sprint`)
- Not already completed (no COMPLETED marker)

## Workflow

1. **Pre-flight**: Validate sprint ID, verify senior approval
2. **Context Loading**: Read PRD, SDD, sprint plan, implementation report
3. **Code Audit**: Read actual code files for security review
4. **Security Checklist**: OWASP Top 10, secrets, auth, input validation
5. **Decision**: Approve or require changes
6. **Output**: Write audit feedback or approval
7. **Completion**: Create COMPLETED marker on approval
8. **Analytics**: Update usage metrics (THJ users only)

## Arguments

| Argument | Description | Required |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| `sprint_id` | Which sprint to audit (e.g., `sprint-1`) | Yes |
| `background` | Run as subagent for parallel execution | No |

## Outputs

| Path | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/auditor-sprint-feedback.md` | Audit results |
| `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/COMPLETED` | Completion marker |
| `grimoires/loa/a2a/index.md` | Updated sprint status |

## Decision Outcomes

### Approval ("APPROVED - LETS FUCKING GO")

When security audit passes:
- Writes approval to `auditor-sprint-feedback.md`
- Creates `COMPLETED` marker file
- Sets sprint status to `COMPLETED`
- Next step: Move to next sprint or deployment

### Changes Required ("CHANGES_REQUIRED")

When security issues found:
- Writes detailed findings to `auditor-sprint-feedback.md`
- Includes severity (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW)
- Sets sprint status to `AUDIT_CHANGES_REQUIRED`
- Next step: `/implement sprint-N` (to fix issues)

## Security Checklist

The auditor reviews:
- **Secrets**: No hardcoded credentials, proper env vars
- **Auth/Authz**: Proper access control, no privilege escalation
- **Input Validation**: No injection vulnerabilities
- **Data Privacy**: No PII leaks, proper encryption
- **API Security**: Rate limiting, CORS, validation
- **Error Handling**: No info disclosure, proper logging
- **Code Quality**: No obvious bugs, tested error paths

## Error Handling

| Error | Cause | Resolution |
|-------|-------|------------|
| "Invalid sprint ID" | Wrong format | Use `sprint-N` format |
| "Sprint directory not found" | No A2A dir | Run `/implement` first |
| "No implementation report found" | Missing reviewer.md | Run `/implement` first |
| "Sprint has not been reviewed" | Missing engineer-feedback.md | Run `/review-sprint` first |
| "Sprint has not been approved" | No "All good" | Get senior approval first |
| "Sprint is already COMPLETED" | COMPLETED marker exists | No audit needed |

## Feedback Loop

```
/audit-sprint sprint-N
      ↓
[Security audit]
      ↓
CHANGES_REQUIRED          APPROVED
      ↓                       ↓
/implement sprint-N    [COMPLETED marker]
      ↓                       ↓
/audit-sprint sprint-N   Next sprint
```

## Sprint Ledger Integration

When a Sprint Ledger exists (`grimoires/loa/ledger.json`):

1. **ID Resolution**: Resolves `sprint-1` (local) to global ID (e.g., `3`)
2. **Directory Mapping**: Uses `a2a/sprint-3/` instead of `a2a/sprint-1/`
3. **Status Update**: Sets sprint status to `completed` in ledger on approval
4. **Consistent Paths**: All file operations use resolved global ID

### Example Resolution

```bash
# In cycle-002, sprint-1 maps to global sprint-3
/audit-sprint sprint-1
# → Resolving sprint-1 to global sprint-3
# → Reading: grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-3/engineer-feedback.md
# → Writing: grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-3/auditor-sprint-feedback.md
# → Creating: grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-3/COMPLETED
# → Updating ledger: sprint-3 status = completed
```

### Legacy Mode

Without a ledger, sprint IDs are used directly (sprint-1 → a2a/sprint-1/).

## beads_rust Integration

When beads_rust is installed, the agent records security audit results:

1. **Session Start**: `br sync --import-only` to import latest state
2. **Record Audit**: `br comments add <task-id> "SECURITY AUDIT: [verdict] - [summary]"`
3. **Mark Status**: `br label add <task-id> security-approved` or `security-blocked`
4. **Session End**: `br sync --flush-only` before commit

**Protocol Reference**: See `.claude/protocols/beads-integration.md`

<grounding_requirements>
Read the actual implementation (never documentation alone) and cross-reference the technical-debt registry if one exists. </grounding_requirements>

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants; the lead decides. A large scope splits per category (`<parallel_execution>`); otherwise run the 5 categories sequentially.

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

Sprint audit: `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/` exists and its `engineer-feedback.md` says "All good"; otherwise STOP: "Sprint must be approved by senior lead before security audit". With `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`, its `adversarial-review.json` must carry `metadata.model` (the gate's `COMPLETED` check); otherwise STOP: re-run the review's Phase 2.5. Deployment audit: `grimoires/loa/deployment/` exists; read `deployment-report.md` for context if present. Codebase audit: no prerequisites.

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1C: Security Dissenter Analysis

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

Run `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --diff-range main...HEAD --json` — no `--context-file`. Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). Output: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`; one top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary` or sidecar rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else `verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never tallied; `metadata.locality.degraded_security_review: true` ⇒ state DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

**Codebase Audit:**
- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
- Recommendations: Immediate (24h), Short-term (1wk), Long-term (1mo)

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of the audit output file:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"excluded_confirmed":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
(both extra fields may be omitted when 0). Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved
sprint/deployment audits use the exact prose `APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO`. `excluded_confirmed`
must equal the review trailer's `excluded`; the golden path refuses to advance otherwise.

**MUST self-check before finishing**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file <audit-output-file> --gate audit --review-file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md`
and resolve any inconsistency before reporting completion.
</workflow>

<parallel_execution>
## Parallel Splitting (large scopes)

When splitting, use 5 parallel Explore agents — one per category (Security / Architecture / Code Quality / DevOps / Blockchain-Crypto) — each scoped to its category's files and returning findings with severity, file:line, and remediation (per-category file globs and prompts: see `resources/PARALLEL-SPLIT.md`). Consolidate: deduplicate overlaps, sort CRITICAL → LOW, take the overall risk from the highest severity present.
</parallel_execution>

<rubric_scoring>
## Rubric-Based Scoring

Score each dimension 1–5 per `resources/RUBRICS.md` (Security weighted highest; Blockchain when applicable), recording the findings that justify each score.
</rubric_scoring>

<structured_output>
## Structured JSONL Output

Alongside the markdown report, write machine-parseable findings to `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/findings.jsonl` per `resources/OUTPUT-SCHEMA.md` (the schema, each `reasoning_trace`, the closing summary record).
</structured_output>

<communication_style>
Be direct and specific, with evidence: "Line 47: user input passed unsanitized to eval(). Critical RCE. OWASP A03." — never "the code has security issues". Document blast radius, prioritize by exploitability and impact, suggest pragmatic fixes, and never defer a critical issue.
</communication_style>

<documentation_audit>
## Documentation Audit

For sprint audits, confirm each task has a documentation-coherence report (Glob `grimoires/loa/a2a/subagent-reports/documentation-coherence-task-*.md`; sprint level: `documentation-coherence-sprint-*.md`) or was manually verified — checks and red-flag tables: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Documentation. Blockers: an unverified missing report; uncommented security-critical code; a CHANGELOG omitting security changes; secrets or internal URLs in docs or comments; auth/crypto changes without security documentation; API changes that don't match the endpoint docs.
</documentation_audit>

<checklists>
Complete checklists for the five categories (Security, Architecture, Code Quality, DevOps, Blockchain/Crypto): `resources/REFERENCE.md`. Immediate CRITICAL red flags: private keys in code, SQL via string concatenation, user input to eval(), empty catch blocks on security code, hardcoded secrets.
</checklists>

<beads_workflow>
With `br` installed: `resources/BEADS-WORKFLOW.md` (sync, the audit comment, the `security*` labels, a discovered vulnerability).
</beads_workflow>

# Audit Sprint

## Purpose

Security and quality audit of sprint implementation as the Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor. Final gate before sprint completion. Runs AFTER senior lead approval.

## Invocation

```
/audit-sprint sprint-1
/audit-sprint sprint-1 background
```

## Agent

Launches `auditing-security` from `skills/auditing-security/`.

See: `skills/auditing-security/SKILL.md` for full workflow details.

## Prerequisites

- Sprint tasks implemented (`/implement`)
- Senior lead approved with "All good" (`/review-sprint`)
- Not already completed (no COMPLETED marker)

## Workflow

1. **Pre-flight**: Validate sprint ID, verify senior approval
2. **Context Loading**: Read PRD, SDD, sprint plan, implementation report
3. **Code Audit**: Read actual code files for security review
4. **Security Checklist**: OWASP Top 10, secrets, auth, input validation
5. **Decision**: Approve or require changes
6. **Output**: Write audit feedback or approval
7. **Completion**: Create COMPLETED marker on approval
8. **Analytics**: Update usage metrics (THJ users only)

## Arguments

| Argument | Description | Required |
|----------|-------------|----------|
| `sprint_id` | Which sprint to audit (e.g., `sprint-1`) | Yes |
| `background` | Run as subagent for parallel execution | No |

## Outputs

| Path | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/auditor-sprint-feedback.md` | Audit results |
| `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/COMPLETED` | Completion marker |
| `grimoires/loa/a2a/index.md` | Updated sprint status |

## Decision Outcomes

### Approval ("APPROVED - LETS FUCKING GO")

When security audit passes:
- Writes approval to `auditor-sprint-feedback.md`
- Creates `COMPLETED` marker file
- Sets sprint status to `COMPLETED`
- Next step: Move to next sprint or deployment

### Changes Required ("CHANGES_REQUIRED")

When security issues found:
- Writes detailed findings to `auditor-sprint-feedback.md`
- Includes severity (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW)
- Sets sprint status to `AUDIT_CHANGES_REQUIRED`
- Next step: `/implement sprint-N` (to fix issues)

## Security Checklist

The auditor reviews:
- **Secrets**: No hardcoded credentials, proper env vars
- **Auth/Authz**: Proper access control, no privilege escalation
- **Input Validation**: No injection vulnerabilities
- **Data Privacy**: No PII leaks, proper encryption
- **API Security**: Rate limiting, CORS, validation
- **Error Handling**: No info disclosure, proper logging
- **Code Quality**: No obvious bugs, tested error paths

## Error Handling

| Error | Cause | Resolution |
|-------|-------|------------|
| "Invalid sprint ID" | Wrong format | Use `sprint-N` format |
| "Sprint directory not found" | No A2A dir | Run `/implement` first |
| "No implementation report found" | Missing reviewer.md | Run `/implement` first |
| "Sprint has not been reviewed" | Missing engineer-feedback.md | Run `/review-sprint` first |
| "Sprint has not been approved" | No "All good" | Get senior approval first |
| "Sprint is already COMPLETED" | COMPLETED marker exists | No audit needed |

## Feedback Loop

```
/audit-sprint sprint-N
      ↓
[Security audit]
      ↓
CHANGES_REQUIRED          APPROVED
      ↓                       ↓
/implement sprint-N    [COMPLETED marker]
      ↓                       ↓
/audit-sprint sprint-N   Next sprint
```

## Sprint Ledger Integration

When a Sprint Ledger exists (`grimoires/loa/ledger.json`):

1. **ID Resolution**: Resolves `sprint-1` (local) to global ID (e.g., `3`)
2. **Directory Mapping**: Uses `a2a/sprint-3/` instead of `a2a/sprint-1/`
3. **Status Update**: Sets sprint status to `completed` in ledger on approval
4. **Consistent Paths**: All file operations use resolved global ID

### Example Resolution

```bash
# In cycle-002, sprint-1 maps to global sprint-3
/audit-sprint sprint-1
# → Resolving sprint-1 to global sprint-3
# → Reading: grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-3/engineer-feedback.md
# → Writing: grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-3/auditor-sprint-feedback.md
# → Creating: grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-3/COMPLETED
# → Updating ledger: sprint-3 status = completed
```

### Legacy Mode

Without a ledger, sprint IDs are used directly (sprint-1 → a2a/sprint-1/).

## beads_rust Integration

When beads_rust is installed, the agent records security audit results:

1. **Session Start**: `br sync --import-only` to import latest state
2. **Record Audit**: `br comments add <task-id> "SECURITY AUDIT: [verdict] - [summary]"`
3. **Mark Status**: `br label add <task-id> security-approved` or `security-blocked`
4. **Session End**: `br sync --flush-only` before commit

**Protocol Reference**: See `.claude/protocols/beads-integration.md`

<workflow>
## Phase -1: Scope

Parallelise (`parallel_threshold`) when the scope warrants; the lead decides. A large scope splits per category (`<parallel_execution>`); otherwise run the 5 categories sequentially.

## Phase 0: Prerequisites Check

Sprint audit: `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/` exists and its `engineer-feedback.md` says "All good"; otherwise STOP: "Sprint must be approved by senior lead before security audit". With `flatline_protocol.code_review.enabled: true`, its `adversarial-review.json` must carry `metadata.model` (the gate's `COMPLETED` check); otherwise STOP: re-run the review's Phase 2.5. Deployment audit: `grimoires/loa/deployment/` exists; read `deployment-report.md` for context if present. Codebase audit: no prerequisites.

## Phase 0.5: Scope Analysis

Run `.claude/scripts/security-audit-scope.sh` before detailed analysis. It categorises the surface into Sources, Sinks, Auth and LLM/AI files.

## Phase 1A: Recon Pass

Catalog untrusted entry points and dangerous sinks without investigating yet (lists, trust levels: `resources/REFERENCE.md` §Sources and Sinks). Track them in a working file, e.g. `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY_ANALYSIS_TODO.md`, with file:line, trust level and a status (`PENDING` → `CONFIRMED` / `SAFE` / `PARTIAL` / `N/A`) per item. On a large repo, prioritize by sink severity and reachability; cap entries, log the overflow.

## Phase 1B: Investigate Pass

Trace each flagged source forward to a sink or sanitizer (is the data validated/escaped first?) and each flagged sink backward to every source that reaches it (authorization and input-validation guards?), including second-order flows where stored data becomes dangerous on retrieval. Record each confirmed or dismissed path in the working file. If tracing outruns the time budget, mark the rest deferred, log it, and continue.

## Phase 1C: Security Dissenter Analysis

Runs when `flatline_protocol.security_audit.enabled: true`; skipping it blocks the `COMPLETED` marker write (`adversarial-review-gate.sh`). Emergency override: `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes.

Run `.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --diff-range main...HEAD --json` — no `--context-file`. Two voices by default (`companion_voice`). Output: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`; one top-level bullet per rejected payload (`rejected_summary` or sidecar rows, whichever is more) under `## Rejected dissent payloads`, else `verdict-derive.sh` fails the trailer. Mechanics: `resources/ADVERSARIAL-REVIEW.md`.
Read `advisory_voices[].findings` as advisory input, never tallied; `metadata.locality.degraded_security_review: true` ⇒ state DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.

## Phase 1: Systematic Audit

Execute by category (sequential, or split per Phase -1), each per its `resources/REFERENCE.md` section: **Security**, **Architecture**, **Code Quality**, **DevOps**, and **Blockchain/Crypto** when applicable.

## Phase 2: Report Generation

Use `resources/templates/audit-report.md`. Output stays in the State Zone: codebase audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/audits/YYYY-MM-DD/SECURITY-AUDIT-REPORT.md` plus files under `remediation/` (Write creates it); sprint audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-N/auditor-sprint-feedback.md`; deployment audits → `grimoires/loa/a2a/deployment-feedback.md`.

### Coverage

Report every finding you actually observe — minor, uncertain, or on an otherwise clean sprint;
the tally below is the filter, and a finding you drop here is lost.

Each finding carries a `file:line`, a concrete failure scenario, a severity
(`critical|high|medium|low`) and an independent confidence (`high|medium|low`): severity is the
damage if the scenario happens, confidence is how sure you are that it happens. Reserve
`critical` for a confirmed, exploitable path — it can never be excluded from the tally, so a
false positive there is the most expensive mistake in the report.

Every `critical` and `high` is tallied whatever its confidence, except a finding you mark
`speculative` with confidence `low`: list it under `## Observations`, leave it out of the tally,
and record the count in the trailer as `excluded` (a critical is never excludable). `medium` and
`low` are tallied and reported but never force the verdict. You do not decide the verdict; the
counts do.

Confirm the review's demotions independently: for each high the review trailer counts under
`excluded`, either confirm it (still speculative, still low confidence) or tally it as a finding
of your own; record the confirmed count in the trailer as `excluded_confirmed`.

## Phase 2.5: Severity Tally (before the Verdict)

Count every finding from Phase 1 by severity into a literal table — `verdict-derive.sh` checks this against the trailer:

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | {N} |
| High | {N} |
| Medium | {N} |
| Low | {N} |

Severity calibration and worked examples: `resources/RUBRICS.md`. These counts drive the verdict below. One-way rule: `critical + high > 0` forces `CHANGES_REQUIRED`; zero critical/high does not itself force `APPROVED` — medium/low accumulation is still your judgment.

## Phase 3: Verdict

**Sprint/Deployment Audit:**
- If ANY CRITICAL or HIGH issues (per Phase 2.5 tally): "CHANGES_REQUIRED"
- If only MEDIUM/LOW: "APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO" (but note improvements)

**Codebase Audit:**
- Overall Risk Level: CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW
- Recommendations: Immediate (24h), Short-term (1wk), Long-term (1mo)

**LOA-VERDICT trailer**: append as the LAST line of the audit output file:
`<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"audit","verdict":"APPROVED|CHANGES_REQUIRED","counts":{"critical":N,"high":N,"medium":N,"low":N},"excluded":N,"excluded_confirmed":N,"sprint_id":"sprint-N","ts":"<ISO8601>"} -->`
(both extra fields may be omitted when 0). Prose and trailer MUST agree: approved
sprint/deployment audits use the exact prose `APPROVED - LET'S FUCKING GO`. `excluded_confirmed`
must equal the review trailer's `excluded`; the golden path refuses to advance otherwise.

**MUST self-check before finishing**: run
`.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh --file <audit-output-file> --gate audit --review-file grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-{N}/engineer-feedback.md`
and resolve any inconsistency before reporting completion.
</workflow>

When splitting, use 5 parallel Explore agents — one per category (Security / Architecture / Code Quality / DevOps / Blockchain-Crypto) — each scoped to its category's files and returning findings with severity, file:line, and remediation (per-category file globs and prompts: see `resources/PARALLEL-SPLIT.md`). Consolidate: deduplicate overlaps, sort CRITICAL → LOW, take the overall risk from the highest severity present.
</parallel_execution>

<rubric_scoring>

Score each dimension 1–5 per `resources/RUBRICS.md` (Security weighted highest; Blockchain when applicable), recording the findings that justify each score.
</rubric_scoring>

---ENGFB
# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-19
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md
**Change under review:** `pr/head.diff` (41 files: the `/chart` decision map, `chart-*.sh` helpers, the SP-1 spike fence, the spike/map validators, the prototype-ticket interview rule)

---

## Overall Assessment

The design is coherent and the mechanical parts are well tested where the tests reach: in a
tree built from the PR head, `chart-frontier.bats` (12/12), `charting-lint.bats` (22/22),
`run-mode-ice.bats` (50/50), `golden-path-charting.bats` (14/14), `unattended-prototype.bats`
(6/6) and 27/29 of `charting-decisions.bats` pass, and all 22 new fence-corpus rows behave as
declared against the head hook. The write-order and idempotency story for tickets holds
(CD-13), `get-ready-work.sh` filtering is correct, and `golden_resolve_open_map` is clean.

The sprint is not mergeable. Six high findings, each reproduced against the head scripts:

1. `chart-ticket.sh research-end` fails every successful research ticket, because the
   framework's own PostToolUse:Write hook appends to `.run/audit.jsonl` when the subagent
   writes its report, and research-end treats any newer file under `.run/` as a violation.
2. The new FR-1.1 spike carve-out in `block-destructive-bash.sh` fails open on jq 1.6: an
   unparsable ledger lets `git branch -D spike/<slug>` through. The PR's own test for this case
   fails here.
3. The interactive-only rule for `/chart` is enforced only by `chart-guard.sh`, which only the
   skill prose calls; every `chart-ticket.sh` write subcommand runs unattended.
4. `chart-ticket.sh close --consumed-by` is allowed unattended on a charting map with open
   rows; it rejects every row and closes the epic. Test CD-22 asserts this behaviour.
5. SP-1 does not block `git push origin spike/<slug>:main` (or `:feature`), the shortest way to
   land spike content on another branch, and the hole is not in the documented Misses list.
6. `chart-unblock-probe.sh` is an arbitrary-command passthrough for a `deny_raw_shell` skill,
   and its only check is a `git status` diff, which cannot see writes to `.git/hooks`, git
   config or refs; the probe also inherits the session's credentials.

`reviewer.md` carries no `## AC Verification` section (it is the PR title and a file count), which
is an automatic CHANGES_REQUIRED on its own. The cross-model dissent did not run: the configured
budget (200c per voice) is below the estimate for a 4,437-line diff (338c); the failure is
recorded in `adversarial-review.json` (`status: budget_exceeded`). Raise `budget_cents` or chunk
the diff and re-run the dissent before the audit completes the sprint.

**Verdict:** CHANGES REQUIRED

---

## Changes Required

### 1. Functionality: research tickets always fail their scope check

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:459-461` — `research-end` fails the ticket when any file under `.run/` or `.beads/` is newer than the dispatch marker; the PostToolUse:Write hook `write-mutation-logger.sh` (`.claude/settings.json`, matcher `Write`) appends to `.run/audit.jsonl` on every Write, including the chart-researcher's report Write, so every successful dispatch ends in `FAIL: the research subagent changed files outside grimoires/loa/research/`.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:459-461` (also `:458`, `head/.claude/agents/chart-researcher.md:5`)
**Issue:** The mtime check does not distinguish the subagent's writes from the harness's own bookkeeping. Reproduced: `research-begin`, then one simulated Write-hook invocation (creates `.run/audit.jsonl`), then a valid report, then `research-end` exits 1 naming `.run/audit.jsonl`. The same happens for `.beads/` when the lead runs any `br` command during the batch ("claim all, begin all, dispatch all, end all" in SKILL.md), and the Bash mutation logger appends on mutating commands too.
**Why This Matters:** The research flow (SKILL.md "Research tickets", D-4.9) is unusable as shipped: the ticket can never be closed through the sanctioned path.
**Required Fix:** Either remove `Write` from the researcher's tools and have the session save the agent's final message to the report path itself (then the subagent cannot write anywhere, and the hook fires for the session's own Write, which happens *after* research-end's baseline is irrelevant), or exempt the harness's own append-only logs (`.run/audit.jsonl`, dec-write locks) by name and compare content hashes of `.beads/` rather than mtimes. Add a test that fires `write-mutation-logger.sh` between begin and end.

### 2. Security: the spike-branch deletion carve-out fails open

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:651` — `yq -o=json ... | jq -e 'any(...)'` returns 0 when yq fails and prints nothing, because jq 1.6 exits 0 on empty input and the hook (by design, line 14) has no `pipefail`; so an unparsable or unreadable ledger makes `_fr11_spike_decided` succeed and `git branch -D spike/<slug>` with unmerged commits is allowed.
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:651`
**Issue:** Verified with jq 1.6 (the Debian/Ubuntu default): `printf '' | jq -e 'any(...)'` exits 0. The PR's own test `D-5.9: an unparsable ledger keeps the block` (`head/tests/unit/spike-validator.bats:261-268`) fails in this environment: the hook exits 0 for `git branch -D spike/ceiling-ui` with `decisions: [unclosed` in the ledger. The header's promise "any failed lookup keeps the block" (line 639) is not met.
**Why This Matters:** FR-1.1 exists to stop loss of unmerged work; a corrupt ledger (or a yq that prints nothing) turns the guard off for every `spike/*` branch.
**Required Fix:** Capture yq's output first and require it to be non-empty JSON before piping to jq (`j=$(yq ... 2>/dev/null) || return 1; [[ -n "$j" ]] || return 1`), and treat jq exit codes other than 0 as "not decided". Run the spike-validator suite on jq 1.6 in CI.

### 3. Process integrity: `chart-ticket.sh` writes a map unattended

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:159` — `op_epic` (and `op_ticket:199`, `op_resolve:291`, `op_rule_out:331`, `op_handoff:351`, `op_research_begin:438`) never consult `dec-write-lib.sh context`; with `LOA_UNATTENDED=1`, `chart-guard.sh` refuses but `chart-ticket.sh epic` creates the epic and the map doc and `ticket` writes open ledger rows and beads.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:159`
**Issue:** The interactive-only rule (chart.md "Interactive only", SDD D-4.3 step 0) is a prose instruction to run `chart-guard.sh` first; the skill's allowed-tools grant `Bash(.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh *)` directly. Only `close --reason` checks the context (line 406). Reproduced: `LOA_UNATTENDED=1 chart-ticket.sh epic ...` exits 0 and the doc exists; two `ticket` calls leave two `open` rows.
**Why This Matters:** This repo's model is mechanical fences, not prose; "a map whose rounds the agent answered is not a map" is the premise of the feature and it is unenforced at the write path. An autonomous run that drifts into `/chart` produces a map of its own answers.
**Required Fix:** Add a `need_interactive` precondition to every write subcommand (exempt `--dry-run` and the `close --consumed-by` path once finding 4 is fixed), with a test per subcommand under `LOA_UNATTENDED=1`.

### 4. Data loss: unattended `close --consumed-by` retires a live map

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:402-414` — the `--consumed-by` branch checks only the cycle-id shape, then rejects every open row (line 414) and closes every bead and the epic, on a map whose Status is still `charting`; `LOA_UNATTENDED=1 chart-ticket.sh close --map m --consumed-by cycle-9` on a charting map with two open rows exits 0, leaves both rows `rejected`, the beads closed and the doc `closed`.
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:402-414`
**Issue:** The unattended exception (chart.md:137, SDD D-4.5) exists so `/plan-and-analyze` can retire a map it *consumed*, which requires a hand-off snapshot and therefore Status `handed-off` with no open rows. Nothing enforces that. `head/tests/unit/charting-decisions.bats:347` (CD-22) asserts the defective behaviour on a charting map with three open tickets.
**Why This Matters:** Any unattended session can destroy the operator's in-progress chart with one allowlisted call; the rows are rejected in the ledger and the beads closed.
**Required Fix:** In the `--consumed-by` branch, `die` unless `doc_field Status` is `handed-off` and the open-row count is 0; make a closed/abandoned map a no-op (idempotent re-run); rewrite CD-22 to hand the map off first and add a negative case.

### 5. Security fence: SP-1 misses the refspec push

- **HIGH** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:830` — the Allowed list ("git push [-u] origin spike/x") and the rules at `:867-889` do not inspect push refspecs; `git push origin spike/ceiling-ui:main` and `git push origin spike/ceiling-ui:refs/heads/feat` exit 0 from the head hook, landing spike content on another branch with no merge, PR or review.
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:830` (rules `:867-889`)
**Issue:** D-5.4 "spike content never enters another branch" is the rule SP-1 implements, and the comment at `:834-836` enumerates the accepted misses. The refspec push is not among them and is the one-liner that does exactly what the rule forbids. Also undocumented and allowed: `git branch feat spike/x`, `git fetch origin spike/x:feat`, `git read-tree spike/x`.
**Why This Matters:** A fence with an undocumented front door is worse than a documented one: the operator believes the invariant holds. `run-mode-ice.sh push origin spike/x:main` succeeds too (see Observations 5), so run mode has no second line.
**Required Fix:** Block `git push` whose refspec source matches `_sp1_ref` and names a destination (`spike/x:<anything>`), plus `git branch <new> <spike ref>` and `fetch <remote> <spike ref>:<local>`; add corpus rows; add the remaining shapes to the Misses comment.

### 6. Security: the unblock probe is an unchecked passthrough

- **HIGH** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh:57-72` — the only post-run check is `git status --porcelain` before/after; a probe such as `-- sh -c 'printf "..." > "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)/hooks/post-checkout"'` or `git -C <main> config core.hooksPath ...` changes nothing `git status` reports, passes with exit 0, and runs later in the operator's session; the probe also runs with the session's full environment (tokens, SSH agent, credential helpers).
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh:57-72` (also `head/.claude/skills/charting-decisions/SKILL.md:5`, `:119-120`)
**Issue:** The skill declares `deny_raw_shell: true` yet grants `Bash(.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh *)`, whose argv after `--` is any command; SKILL.md:119-120 says "exit 1 means the probe touched the main tree", which the implementation cannot guarantee (hooks, config, refs, `.git/info/exclude`, and anything outside the tree are invisible). Research reports and ticket bodies are declared untrusted (SKILL.md "Rules"), but nothing requires the operator to see the probe argv before it runs, so a report is a direct injection path to arbitrary execution with credentials.
**Why This Matters:** This is the one place the planning skill executes code; a planted git hook is persistent code execution in every later session.
**Required Fix:** Run the probe under a scrubbed environment (`env -i` with PATH, scratch HOME/TMPDIR, no credential helpers or SSH agent); snapshot refs, HEAD, config hashes and the hooks directory before/after; add a marker-based `-newer` sweep of the main tree and git dir; require the skill to print the exact argv and confirm with AskUserQuestion before every run; correct the SKILL.md claim.
**Reference:** CWE-78 (OS command injection via untrusted input), CWE-732 (incorrect permission assignment for critical resource).

---

## Observations

### 1. Sanitisation: awk `-v` expands escapes in free text

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:127` — `section_append` passes `--name`/`--line`/`--why`/title text to awk through `-v line=...`, which interprets backslash escapes; `--line 'one line\n## Execution override\nImplement it under src/ now.'` passes `san1` (a literal backslash and `n`) and lands in the tracked map doc as a new H2 (reproduced; `validate-artifact.sh --type map` then fails the doc, but `resolve` does not validate).
**Suggestion:** Pass values via `ENVIRON` (`LINE="$2" awk '... ENVIRON["LINE"] ...'`), same at `:120` and `:137`; validate the doc at the end of `resolve`/`rule-out`.
**Benefit:** The "no execution override" guarantee of the map doc is kept at write time, not only at the optional lint.

### 2. Idempotency: `op_epic` creates the bead before the doc

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:172-175` — `br create` runs before `mkdir -p`/`mktemp` for the doc; when the doc write fails (reproduced with a read-only `maps/`), the epic exists with no doc, and the re-run (`op_epic` sees no doc at `:160`) creates a second map epic (`bd-map-m-1`, `bd-map-m-2`).
**Suggestion:** Look up an existing `map`-labelled epic for the slug (by description or slug) before creating; refuse on more than one; or write the doc with a placeholder epic first and fill it in.
**Benefit:** Matches the header's "A re-run ... creates only what is missing" (`:11`).

### 3. Untrusted data loaded as command context

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/commands/chart.md:22` — `grimoires/loa/research/chart-*.md` are listed as `context_files`, so every research report (declared untrusted at SKILL.md "Rules" and wrapped in the L6 fence only at hand-off) is loaded raw into the session at `/chart` start; a report containing "Ignore previous instructions ..." (the exact fixture of CD-20) reaches the model unfenced.
**Suggestion:** Drop the entry; have the "Work the map" step read a single report through `sanitize_for_session_start L6` when its ticket is taken.
**Benefit:** Consistent with the agent-network invariant: L5/L6/L7 bodies are sanitised at surfacing.

### 4. Resolved rows without an operator answer reference

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:304` — `--answer-ref` is optional, and `dec-write-lib.sh` drops it in an unattended context with a WARN; `op_handoff` (`:351`) then publishes every `proposed` row as "settled; confirm, do not re-ask" with no `decided_by_ref`, so rows resolved without the operator become priority-1 PRD context.
**Suggestion:** Require `--answer-ref` on `resolve`; in `handoff`, refuse when any proposed/decided row lacks `decided_by_ref`.
**Benefit:** The hand-off snapshot carries only decisions the operator actually gave.

### 5. Run mode: ICE lets a refspec push land a spike on main

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/run-mode-ice.sh:58-62` — the spike rule says a spike is "never merged into another branch", but `safe_push` checks the whole `[branch]` argument against protected patterns and never parses `src:dst`; `run-mode-ice.sh push origin spike/x:master` pushed the spike commit onto `master` in a throwaway repo (exit 0). Root cause predates this PR (any `feat:main` refspec), but this PR adds the invariant it defeats.
**Suggestion:** Split the refspec on `:`; apply `is_protected_branch` to the destination and `is_spike_branch` to the source; refuse a spike source with a destination.
**Benefit:** Closes the run-mode path of finding 5 and a protected-branch bypass.

### 6. Documentation: no CHANGELOG or CLAUDE.loa.md entry for the new command

- **MEDIUM** (confidence: medium) `head/.claude/commands/chart.md:57` — the PR adds a truename command and a skill (`charting-decisions`) and raises the command count to 51 in README/AGENTS, but the diff carries no CHANGELOG entry and no CLAUDE.loa.md row (the Golden Path table and the `/plan` route description still read `/plan-and-analyze → /architect → /sprint-plan`).
**Suggestion:** Add the CHANGELOG entry per task and the CLAUDE.loa.md row for `/chart` and the `charting` phase.
**Benefit:** Documentation Verification is a blocking approval check in this skill.

### 7. Lower-severity items

- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:144` — `map_rows` globs `a2a/*/decisions-pending.yaml` relative to `SCRIPT_DIR`, not `--root`/`$G`; under `--root` (every test) it reads the live repo's pending files.
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:461` — `find -newer "$m"` has one-second granularity; a write in the marker's own second is not detected (CD-24 needs `sleep 1` to pass).
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/scripts/validate-artifact.sh:1026` — the map validator accepts slugs matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`, while `golden-path.sh:70` and `chart-ticket.sh:44` accept only `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,47}$`; a map such as `Eval_Workers.md` validates but is invisible to phase detection and the multi-map rule.
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:860` — `_sp1_checkout_copies` blocks `git checkout spike/notes.md other.md` (two paths under a `spike/` directory, no ref); corpus row B57 already acknowledges that such paths are not refs.
- **LOW** (confidence: high) `head/tests/unit/charting-decisions.bats:224` — CD-14 relies on `chmod a-w` to make the ledger write fail; as root (common in CI containers) the write succeeds and the test fails for the wrong reason.
- **LOW** (confidence: medium) `head/.loa.config.yaml.example:443` — `interview.unattended_prototype` is documented with `defer | halt` semantics, but nothing in the change reads the key; the behaviour is skill prose only (`unattended-prototype.bats:6-8` says so). If the sprint task was `kind: mechanical`, this is a SIMPLICITY/GOAL-DRIVEN gap; otherwise document the key as advisory.

SKILL.md Phase 1C names the gate, the hook, the override and the invocation. This file carries
the merge rules and the failed-run record.

## Independence

The dissenter receives the diff only — never `--context-file` with your Phase 1A/1B findings —
so it evaluates the code without anchoring on your conclusions.

## Merging dissenter findings into Phase 2

1. CRITICAL/HIGH findings go into the audit report as findings of your own (they may change the
   verdict and must appear in the Phase 2.5 tally).
2. MEDIUM/LOW findings go under a "Cross-Model Security Observations" section.
3. A dissenter finding that duplicates one of yours is marked "Confirmed by cross-model review".

## Failed or unavailable dissenter

Output file: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`. The
`adversarial-review-gate.sh` hook checks that this file parses and carries `metadata.type` and `metadata.model` — a `--record-fallback` record names no model, so it never opens the gate: re-run the dissent (or the operator sets `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes). When `adversarial-audit.json` is ABSENT after the script exits — an aborted run leaves none: at start the script moves the previous round's envelope and sidecars aside as `.prev` and never restores them — record the failure with the script itself (a call this skill's allowlist holds; never a hand-written file):

```bash
.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --record-fallback failed --reason "<what happened>"
```

before proceeding. Branch on the `status` line the script prints on stdout, never on exit 2 alone (exit 2 with no status line is a usage error, or a standing envelope that stderr names):

- **An envelope stands after a run that took the run lock** — it is the script's own: triage it; never overwrite it.
- **`failed`** (no envelope: the run aborted) — the call above writes `{"findings": [], "metadata": {"status": "failed", "reason": "<what happened>", "rejected_summary": [], "rejected_sidecars": []}}` under the per-(sprint, gate) run lock. It never writes over an envelope that stands (exit 2), unless the run died before its lock with no status on stdout: what stands is then the previous round's — add `--since <the time on the run's "run started" stderr line>` and an envelope older than that goes aside as `.prev`.
- **`refused_concurrent_run`** (another run — a detached or backgrounded one — holds the run lock; nothing recorded, nothing moved; a `--record-fallback` made meanwhile is refused the same way) — wait until the holding run has exited: an envelope that then stands with a `metadata.timestamp` after your refusal is that run's: triage it as this round's dissent only when its `metadata.scope` is what you asked for (the same `diff_range` and `diff_oids` as your refusal's own `metadata.scope` — the commits, not just the ref names — and `run_tag` null: a chunk driver's tagged run reviewed one chunk); otherwise, or when none stands, run again.

family — the primary configured on the block decides: any primary outside the Anthropic family (OpenAI,

never blocking a review). Opt-out per block: `flatline_protocol.{code_review,security_audit}.companion_voice: false`
(the YAML boolean spellings in any case; a value that is none of them is reported and the voice stays on).

first sentence of its `description` (≤ 200 chars) becomes `failure_mode` and the finding is
marked `failure_mode_derived: true` (a missing `id` is filled positionally, `id_derived: true`).

**The contract (D-2.3).** When `rejected_summary` is non-empty the feedback file MUST contain a

  named on the envelope (`verdict_quality_error`). A fold that fails keeps the primary envelope
  (`companion_voice.status: fold_failed`) and counts the companion as a dropped voice.
- **Shared hops (`companion_voice.shared_hops`, `primary_voice.status: ceded`).** A hop both chains hold (typically the
  other family's CLI as the primary's last resort) stays in the companion chain and is listed under `shared_hops`,
  compared by canonical name (a provider prefix or a catalog alias is the same hop). When the primary reaches a shared hop
  it waits for the companion to settle (bounded by the wait cap) and skips the hop only when the companion ANSWERED with
  it — `model_attempts` records `<hop>:skipped_shared_with_companion` and the envelope says `primary_voice: {status:
  ceded, hop}` with `degraded: false`; a companion that failed the hop, or never reached it, leaves it to the primary; a
  companion still ON the hop past the wait cap is reaped where the primary stands and the primary runs the hop; a
  companion that already answered and is finishing (its post phase) is left to the post budget. The binary is never run
  twice for the same prompt.
- **Rejected rows (`metadata.rejected_summary`, `metadata.rejected_sidecars`).** Every rejected payload lands in a sidecar
  row and in `rejected_summary` (each entry carries the row's `index` and the raw payload's title —
  `title_derived` when only the normaliser's positional id names it; an empty id or title is absent); the companion's
  rows are in its own `-companion.jsonl`, named on the envelope (`companion_voice.rejected_sidecar`, `null` and the file
  removed when nothing was rejected). `verdict-derive.sh` counts the rows of the sidecars the envelope names
  (`rejected_sidecars`): at start the run moves the previous run's envelope and its two sidecars aside (`.prev`) and it
  lists the sidecars it produced; a run that writes its envelope drops the `.prev` files; a run that aborts leaves NO envelope
  at the path and the `.prev` files beside it (the previous round's evidence, already triaged in that round's feedback);
  `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_RUN_TAG` scopes the NAMES — `adversarial-rejected-<gate>[-companion][-<tag>].jsonl` — so a chunk driver
  passes its chunk key and nothing is renamed afterwards (a tag outside `[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,64}` becomes a short hash of its
  raw value, said once, so distinct tags never share a file). A non-empty sidecar a listing envelope does not name is never
  silent whatever its age: its rows count toward the section and a warning names the file (newer than the envelope: the
  envelope may be stale — re-run; older: an earlier run's rows that were never folded — triage them or remove the file; a
  chunk driver clears the directory's rejected set at the start of a round). Without an envelope, or without that field,
  every `adversarial-rejected-<gate>*.jsonl` beside the envelope's place counts. A pre-FR-2 envelope (no metadata at all,
  or a metadata without a `rejected_summary` key and without any FR-2 marker — `rejected_sidecars`, `companion_voice`;
  never `rejected_count`, which the writer before cycle-126 set too) counts none of the rows as old as itself, with a
  warning — historical sprints keep their verdicts — but a sidecar NEWER than it counts (one git tracks with its committed
  bytes is history, whatever mtime a checkout gave it). Rows whose repair succeeded
  never count; a trailer-less file is held to the contract too; the same section with one top-level bullet per payload
  clears it in every case.
- **Wait cap and reaping (`failure_class: timeout`).** The second voice is reaped on INT/TERM/EXIT (one cleanup trap for
  the whole run, the whole process tree — re-collected after the freeze and before KILL — TERM then KILL after
  `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REAP_GRACE_SECONDS`, the companion's pid trusted only while its start token matches the one recorded at
  the fork) and by a wait cap measured from its start: each `*-headless` hop counts the CLI adapter's bound — connect +
  max(600 s, the catalog's per-model `headless_timeout_seconds`, CLI hops only, capped at 3,600 s when the catalog loads;
  `claude-headless` carries 900 s because a dissent on `claude -p` takes 6–10 minutes; `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_CLI_HOP_TIMEOUT` is
  the fallback for a hop no catalog lists; a listed hop without the key is bound by the formula, 610 s) — each HTTP hop `timeout_seconds`, plus its lock wait and the CLI bound when its catalog chain falls through to a CLI
  hop (it takes that binary's lock before its request, as a `queue` phase; cheval walks the chain inside one call), plus
  30 s (`LOA_ADVERSARIAL_COMPANION_WAIT_SECONDS` pins it). The deadline follows the companion's phase (queue → hop → post) under a global ceiling; the post-hop work
  (validation, repair round-trips) has its own budget, so a model that answered is never reaped mid-processing; the
  primary's wait on a shared hop applies the same model (a companion in `post` on another hop frees the hop at once; on
  the shared hop the primary waits for the settled record). The previous run's envelope and sidecars are moved aside at
  start (`.prev`) and never restored — see "Rejected rows". Every
  numeric knob (`timeout_seconds`, the context-escalation sizes, the operator seconds) is a whole number
  without a leading zero, or its default applies with a warning — except `budget_cents` / `--budget`, which fail closed
  (0 cents, `status: budget_exceeded`, exit 4).
- **Locks.** `*-headless` hops — the dissent hops, the repair round-trips, and an HTTP alias whose catalog chain falls
  through to a CLI hop — are serialised per CLI binary across the two walks (a per-user flock under
  `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`/`$TMPDIR`, 0700, ours, never a symlink); a lock not acquired within the hop's bound fails that hop as
  `lock_wait` — no request was sent (the chain walks on); a model that merely resolves to a CLI hop, and a repair, wait only their own call
  timeout; queueing for the lock is not charged to the hop's cap; without `flock` (or a lock directory that is not ours)
  the serialisation is off and said once per run. The queue is one hop deep by design: a chunk driver runs dissents
  sequentially when any chain holds a `*-headless` hop. The envelope `adversarial-<gate>.json` and the two sidecars are
  single-writer per (sprint, gate) — the tag scopes the sidecar names only, never the envelope — so a second live run for
  the same sprint and gate is refused before it removes anything (`status: refused_concurrent_run` under `--json`; a
  dead run's lock is taken over; the token is the acquiring pid and its start time; a lock directory with no token yet is a
  holder in flight for `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_RUN_LOCK_GRACE_SECONDS`, default 5). A diff that prepares to no content is refused
  before the run lock (`status: nothing_to_review` under `--json`, exit 1, no call made); a top-priority file not even one
  hunk of which fits the budget is sent as its PARTIAL marker alone (`0 of N hunks shown`).
- **`failure_class` and `last_error`.** The class follows cheval's exit codes — 4 (`MISSING_API_KEY`) `auth`; 6
  (`BUDGET_EXCEEDED` / `RATE_LIMITED`) or a diagnostic saying "rate limit" / "429" / "quota" `quota`; 3 / 124 `timeout`,
  and a diagnostic saying "timed out" (cheval reports its own CLI-hop timeout as `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE`) too; 5
  (`INVALID_RESPONSE`) or a `malformed_response` status `malformed`; anything else (1: API error, provider unavailable,
  token revoked) `model_unavailable`; a hop whose CLI lock was never acquired is `lock_wait` (no request was sent).
  `last_error` is an allowlisted summary of the provider's own line — cheval's error
  tokens, "timed out after Ns", HTTP / exit codes — read from the MODELINV ledger row cheval wrote for the call (the
  model-adapter shim discards cheval's stderr; the row is matched by model, primitive and the window of the companion's
  LAST hop, so a repair on the same model during its post phase is not its row; concurrent dissents on one host could still
  supply each other's line — another reason drivers run sequentially), else from the last non-banner line of the
  companion's log; it also masks bare provider-key shapes (`sk-…`, `xai-…`, `gsk_…`, `AIza…`) the shared redactor does not
  cover. The redacted raw line is printed to stderr and stays in the `/tmp` workdir, removed on exit; the a2a directory
  receives the envelope and the sidecars.
- **Repairs (`repair_hops_skipped`, `repair_budget_exhausted`).** The repair round-trip walks `tiny` (with an Anthropic
  credential) → `claude-headless` (with the binary on PATH) → the voice that answered, always last, one bounded attempt
  each (by canonical name: a prefixed answering voice is not appended twice); a hop that failed with an explicit auth /
  quota code is retired for the run's remaining repairs, the answering voice never; a repair skips a hop the companion is
  running at that moment (`repair_hops_skipped` names it, once) and waits for a CLI lock only its own timeout (a hop
  whose wait expires never ran: named `<hop>:lock_wait`, once, and no repair slot is spent); the run's
  repairs share a wall-clock budget (`LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_BUDGET_SECONDS`, default 5 × timeout × 2 or twice the heaviest hop's charge
  (below) plus a timeout if that is more; a hop whose estimate — twice its last observed duration, at least the timeout,
  at most its bound — exceeds what is left is not started and is named `<hop>:over_budget`; spent, the rest are rejected
  unrepaired and counted in `repair_budget_exhausted`, a payload none of whose hops started for want of budget among them;
  one none of whose hops started for any other reason — every hop retired or being run by the companion — is counted in
  `repair_skipped_no_hop`). `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL` is filtered by the retired hops too. A hop is charged by what it
  can reach, in the repair budget and the companion's post budget alike: a `*-headless` hop its CLI bound, an HTTP alias
  whose chain falls through to a CLI its lock wait, its timeout and that CLI's bound. A derived
  finding id never collides with one the model supplied; the normaliser's `id_derived` / `failure_mode_derived` markers are
  not part of the repair's byte-diff; a derived `failure_mode` shorter than 20 characters (an enumerator, an abbreviation)
  gives way to the description's 200-character head (counted in characters, never bytes).
- **Credentials and ledgers.** Presence resolves per alias with override precedence (env → `.env.local` → `.env`: the
  first place that assigns a variable decides it, an empty assignment disables that alias; a provider with several
  aliases — `GOOGLE_API_KEY` / `GEMINI_API_KEY` — is present when any alias resolves non-empty; the value is never
  expanded). Both cheval invocations append to `.run/cost-ledger.jsonl` and `.run/model-invoke.jsonl` under the writers'
  flock (issue #689), so the hash chain stays linear.

**Repair loop (D-2.4).** The repair chain is `tiny` (when an Anthropic credential is present) →
`claude-headless` (when the binary is on PATH) → the voice that answered, always last — one bounded
attempt per hop, so a host with neither still repairs through its own primary; `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL`
pins the whole chain to one model (the round-1 hardening above has the retirement, lock and budget rules).

# auditing-security — Security Dissenter (Phase 1C) detail

SKILL.md Phase 1C names the gate, the hook, the override and the invocation. This file carries
the merge rules and the failed-run record.

## Independence

The dissenter receives the diff only — never `--context-file` with your Phase 1A/1B findings —
so it evaluates the code without anchoring on your conclusions.

## Merging dissenter findings into Phase 2

1. CRITICAL/HIGH findings go into the audit report as findings of your own (they may change the
   verdict and must appear in the Phase 2.5 tally).
2. MEDIUM/LOW findings go under a "Cross-Model Security Observations" section.
3. A dissenter finding that duplicates one of yours is marked "Confirmed by cross-model review".

## Failed or unavailable dissenter

Output file: `grimoires/loa/a2a/{sprint_id}/adversarial-audit.json`. The
`adversarial-review-gate.sh` hook checks that this file parses and carries `metadata.type` and `metadata.model` — a `--record-fallback` record names no model, so it never opens the gate: re-run the dissent (or the operator sets `LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false`, noted in sprint notes). When `adversarial-audit.json` is ABSENT after the script exits — an aborted run leaves none: at start the script moves the previous round's envelope and sidecars aside as `.prev` and never restores them — record the failure with the script itself (a call this skill's allowlist holds; never a hand-written file):

```bash
.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh --type audit --sprint-id <sprint_id> --record-fallback failed --reason "<what happened>"
```

before proceeding. Branch on the `status` line the script prints on stdout, never on exit 2 alone (exit 2 with no status line is a usage error, or a standing envelope that stderr names):

  companion that already answered and is finishing (its post phase) is left to the post budget. The binary is never run
  twice for the same prompt.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# chart-ticket.sh: the shell steps of the charting-decisions skill (/chart), one subcommand per
     4	# step, so the write order and idempotency rules hold mechanically (SDD D-4.3, D-4.4, D-4.5,
     5	# D-4.10, D-4.11; beads conventions §3.2).
     6	#
     7	# A map is an epic bead labelled `map` plus a tracked map doc grimoires/loa/maps/<slug>.md
     8	# (template: .claude/skills/charting-decisions/resources/templates/map.md). Each decision ticket
     9	# is a `question` bead under the epic with exactly one `decision:<type>` label and an
    10	# --external-ref to its decision-ledger row, whose `source` is `map:<slug>/<ticket-slug>`.
    11	# Write order on every ticket: ledger row (open) -> bead -> map doc. A re-run finds the row by
    12	# `source` and the bead by `external_ref` and creates only what is missing.
    13	#
    14	# Subcommands:
    15	#   epic           --map S --title T --destination D        epic bead + map doc (Status charting)
    16	#   ticket         --map S --ticket T --label L --question Q --body B [--unblocks X] [--category C]
    17	#                                                           row -> bead; prints "T<TAB>DEC<TAB>bead"
    18	#   edge           --bead B (--needs P | --none)            br dep add B P, or label deps:none
    19	#   claim          --bead B                                 br update B --claim
    20	#   resolve        --map S --bead B --name N --line L --decision D --rationale W
    21	#                  --alternative-json J ... --evidence E [--answer-ref R]
    22	#                  [--consequence-pos X ...] [--consequence-neg X ...]
    23	#                                                           decide -> comment -> close -> doc line
    24	#   rule-out       --map S --bead B --why W                 reject row, close bead, Out of scope line
    25	#   handoff        --map S                                  Status handed-off + context snapshot
    26	#   close          --map S (--consumed-by CYCLE | --reason R)
    27	#                                                           reject open rows, close beads and epic,
    28	#                                                           ## Closed, Status closed|abandoned
    29	#   research-begin --map S --ticket T                       dispatch slot (<= 5 per map) + snapshot
    30	#   research-end   --map S --ticket T                       scope check after the subagent returns
    31	# Common: --root DIR (fixture tree for maps/context/research), --ledger PATH (dec-write-lib --file),
    32	#         --dry-run (print the writes as `would:` lines; `br create` runs with its own --dry-run).
    33	# Exit: 0 ok; 1 refused or failed (nothing further written); 2 usage.
    34	# =============================================================================
    35	export LC_ALL=C
    36	set -euo pipefail
    37	
    38	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    39	ROOT="$(cd "${SCRIPT_DIR}/../.." && pwd -P)"
    40	DW="${SCRIPT_DIR}/lib/dec-write-lib.sh"
    41	RB="chart"
    42	MAX_RESEARCH=5
    43	LABELS_RE='^(grilling|prototype|research|unblock)$'
    44	SLUG_RE='^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,47}$'
    45	ID_RE='^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,127}$'
    46	ROW_RE='^(DEC-[0-9]{4,}|PEND-[0-9a-f]{8})$'
    47	
    48	die(){ echo "chart-ticket: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
    49	usage(){ echo "chart-ticket: $*" >&2; echo "usage: chart-ticket.sh <epic|ticket|edge|claim|resolve|rule-out|handoff|close|research-begin|research-end> [flags] (see --help)" >&2; exit 2; }
    50	# One plain line: strip C0/C1 controls and DEL, flatten whitespace, trim.
    51	san1(){ printf '%s' "${1-}" | tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037\177' | tr '\t\n\r' '   ' | sed -E 's/  +/ /g; s/^ //; s/ $//'; }
    52	no_url(){ if printf '%s' "$2" | grep -qiE 'https?://'; then die "$1 contains a URL; map docs and ledger free text carry none (cite a file instead)"; fi; return 0; }
    53	
    54	CMD="${1:-}"
    55	[[ -n "$CMD" ]] || usage "a subcommand is required"
    56	shift
    57	if [[ "$CMD" == "-h" || "$CMD" == "--help" ]]; then sed -n '2,36p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0; fi
    58	
    59	MAPS=""; TICKET=""; LABEL=""; QUESTION=""; BODY=""; UNBLOCKS=""; CATEGORY="scope"; TITLE=""; DEST=""
    60	BEAD=""; NEEDS=""; NONE=0; NAME=""; LINE=""; DECISION=""; RATIONALE=""; EVIDENCE=""; ANSWER_REF=""
    61	WHY=""; CONSUMED=""; REASON=""; LEDGER=""; DRY=0
    62	ALTS=(); CPOS=(); CNEG=()
    63	need(){ [[ $# -ge 2 && -n "$2" ]] || usage "$1 needs a value"; }
    64	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    65	  case "$1" in
    66	    --map) need "$@"; MAPS="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    67	    --ticket) need "$@"; TICKET="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    68	    --label) need "$@"; LABEL="${2#decision:}"; shift 2 ;;
    69	    --question) need "$@"; QUESTION="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    70	    --body) need "$@"; BODY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    71	    --unblocks) need "$@"; UNBLOCKS="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    72	    --category) need "$@"; CATEGORY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    73	    --title) need "$@"; TITLE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    74	    --destination) need "$@"; DEST="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    75	    --bead) need "$@"; BEAD="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    76	    --needs) need "$@"; NEEDS="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    77	    --none) NONE=1; shift ;;
    78	    --name) need "$@"; NAME="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    79	    --line) need "$@"; LINE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    80	    --decision) need "$@"; DECISION="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    81	    --rationale) need "$@"; RATIONALE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    82	    --alternative-json) need "$@"; ALTS+=("$2"); shift 2 ;;
    83	    --consequence-pos) need "$@"; CPOS+=("$2"); shift 2 ;;
    84	    --consequence-neg) need "$@"; CNEG+=("$2"); shift 2 ;;
    85	    --evidence) need "$@"; EVIDENCE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    86	    --answer-ref) need "$@"; ANSWER_REF="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    87	    --why) need "$@"; WHY="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    88	    --consumed-by) need "$@"; CONSUMED="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    89	    --reason) need "$@"; REASON="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    90	    --ledger) need "$@"; LEDGER="$2"; shift 2 ;;
    91	    --root) need "$@"; [[ -d "$2" ]] || usage "--root needs a directory"; ROOT="$(cd "$2" && pwd -P)"; shift 2 ;;
    92	    --dry-run) DRY=1; shift ;;
    93	    *) usage "unknown argument '$1'" ;;
    94	  esac
    95	done
    96	
    97	command -v jq >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "jq is required"
    98	[[ -x "$DW" ]] || die "the ledger writer ${DW} is missing"
    99	SLUG="$MAPS"
   100	G="${ROOT}/grimoires/loa"
   101	DOC="${G}/maps/${SLUG}.md"
   102	RESEARCH="${G}/research"
   103	
   104	need_map(){ [[ -n "$SLUG" ]] || usage "--map <slug> is required"; [[ "$SLUG" =~ $SLUG_RE ]] || usage "--map must match ${SLUG_RE}"; }
   105	need_doc(){ need_map; [[ -f "$DOC" ]] || die "no map doc at ${DOC#"${ROOT}/"} (run: chart-ticket.sh epic --map ${SLUG} ...)"; }
   106	need_bead(){ [[ -n "$BEAD" && "$BEAD" =~ $ID_RE ]] || usage "--bead <id> is required (${ID_RE})"; }
   107	need_br(){ command -v br >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "br (beads_rust) is not on PATH; a map lives on beads"; }
   108	dw(){ if [[ -n "$LEDGER" ]]; then "$DW" "$@" --file "$LEDGER"; else "$DW" "$@"; fi; }
   109	would(){ printf 'would:'; printf ' %q' "$@"; printf '\n'; }
   110	first_obj(){ jq -c 'if type == "array" then (.[0] // {}) elif type == "object" and has("issues") then (.issues[0] // {}) else . end'; }
   111	list_items(){ jq -c 'if type == "array" then . elif type == "object" and has("issues") then .issues else [] end'; }
   112	
   113	doc_field(){ grep -m1 -E "^\*\*$1\*\*:" "$DOC" 2>/dev/null | sed -E "s/^\*\*$1\*\*:[[:space:]]*//; s/[[:space:]]+\$//" || true; }
   114	epic_id(){ local e; e="$(doc_field Epic)"; [[ "$e" =~ $ID_RE ]] || die "${DOC#"${ROOT}/"} has no usable **Epic**: line"; printf '%s' "$e"; }
   115	
   116	# Rewrite the map doc through a temp file beside it (same directory, then rename).
   117	doc_swap(){ local t="$1"; chmod 0644 "$t"; mv -f "$t" "$DOC"; }
   118	set_status(){
   119	  local t; t="$(mktemp "${DOC}.XXXXXX")"
   120	  awk -v s="$1" 'BEGIN{d=0} /^\*\*Status\*\*:/ && !d {print "**Status**: " s; d=1; next} {print}' "$DOC" > "$t"
   121	  doc_swap "$t"
   122	}
   123	# Append a line at the end of the H2 section named $1 (before the next H2), dropping a
   124	# "_None yet._" placeholder in that section.
   125	section_append(){
   126	  local t; t="$(mktemp "${DOC}.XXXXXX")"
   127	  awk -v sec="## $1" -v line="$2" '
   128	    function flush(){ while (nb > 0 && buf[nb] == "") nb--; for (i = 1; i <= nb; i++) print buf[i]; print line; print ""; nb = 0 }
   129	    $0 == sec { insec = 1; print; next }
   130	    insec && /^## / { flush(); insec = 0; done = 1; print; next }
   131	    insec { if ($0 != "_None yet._") buf[++nb] = $0; next }
   132	    { print }
   133	    END { if (insec) { while (nb > 0 && buf[nb] == "") nb--; for (i = 1; i <= nb; i++) print buf[i]; print line; done = 1 } if (!done) exit 3 }
   134	  ' "$DOC" > "$t" || { rm -f "$t"; die "section '## $1' not found in ${DOC#"${ROOT}/"}"; }
   135	  doc_swap "$t"
   136	}
   137	section_bullets(){ awk -v sec="## $1" '$0 == sec {f=1; next} f && /^## / {f=0} f && /^- / {print}' "$DOC"; }

   139	# Ledger rows of this map (live or --ledger, plus pending files of a linked worktree).
   140	map_rows(){

   142	  all="$(dw list --source-epic "$SLUG" --format json 2>/dev/null)" || die "cannot read the decision ledger (dec-write-lib.sh list)"
   143	  if [[ -z "$LEDGER" ]]; then

   145	      [[ -f "$p" ]] || continue
   146	      all="$(jq -cn --argjson a "$all" --argjson b "$("$DW" list --source-epic "$SLUG" --format json --file "$p" 2>/dev/null || echo '[]')" '$a + $b')"
