# Sprint 1 Security Audit Feedback

**Auditor:** Paranoid Cypherpunk Auditor
**Date:** 2026-10-19
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md
**Change under audit:** `pr/head.diff` (41 files: `/chart` decision maps, `chart-*.sh`, the SP-1 and FR-1.1 spike rules in `block-destructive-bash.sh`, ICE spike handling, map/spike validators, the prototype-ticket rule)

---

## Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED

---

## Executive Summary

The sprint adds a planning surface whose safety story rests on four mechanical fences: the
interactive-only guard, the research-subagent scope check, the unblock-probe sandbox, and the
SP-1/FR-1.1 spike rules. Each of the four is either absent at the path the skill's allowlist
actually grants, defeatable by the party it fences, or fails open on an environment this repo
ships to (jq 1.6). Every high finding below was reproduced against the head scripts in an
isolated tree (`$TMPDIR/ov.G6rmeL`, `$TMPDIR/audit.*`); the reproduction script is
`.eval/tmp/audit-repro.sh`. The cross-model dissent ran with two independent voices
(gpt-5.5-pro via codex-headless, claude-headless), both succeeded, nothing was rejected, and the
companion voice independently reached the marker-rewrite bypass (HIGH-002) and the `--consumed-by`
data-loss path (HIGH-006).

Process note: `engineer-feedback.md` carries `CHANGES REQUIRED`, not "All good", so the Phase 0
prerequisite for a sprint audit is not met. The task brief (`pr/AUDIT-INSTRUCTIONS.md`) directs
the audit to run on the PR files regardless; the verdict below would be `CHANGES_REQUIRED` on the
security findings alone. `reviewer.md` is the PR title and a file count and carries no
`## AC Verification` section.

**Security Issues Found:**

| Severity | Count |
|----------|-------|
| Critical | 0 |
| High | 7 |
| Medium | 8 |
| Low | 9 |

Dissent status: `adversarial-audit.json` `status: reviewed`, `degraded: false`,
`companion_voice.status: succeeded`, `counted_as: independent_voice`, `rejected_summary: []`,
sidecar `adversarial-rejected-audit.jsonl` empty. Not a DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW.
Scope-tool note: `security-audit-scope.sh` over `pr/head/` reports zero sources and sinks (it
looks for web-framework shapes); the recon below was done by hand.

---

## Critical Security Issues (Must Fix)

None.

---

## High Priority Security Issues (Fix Before Deployment)

### [HIGH-001] The unblock probe's sandbox claim is false: shared `.git`, inherited HOME and environment

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh:57-72` (also `:58`, `:66`; `head/.claude/skills/charting-decisions/SKILL.md:5`, `:119-120`)
**Issue:** The helper's only verdict is a before/after string compare of `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching` on the main tree (`:57`, `:71-72`). The probe runs with the session's full environment (`run_with_timeout "$TIMEOUT" "$@"`, `:66`) inside a worktree that shares the main repository's common git directory (`git -C "$MAIN" worktree add --detach`, `:58`). Nothing under `.git/`, nothing in `$HOME`, and nothing outside the repository ever appears in `git status`. SKILL.md:5 grants `Bash(.claude/scripts/chart-unblock-probe.sh *)` to a skill declaring `deny_raw_shell: true`, and SKILL.md:119-120 tells the agent "exit 1 means the probe touched the main tree", with no operator confirmation of the argv.
**Impact:** Persistent code execution. A probe argv chosen under the influence of an untrusted research report or ticket body (both declared untrusted at SKILL.md:160-161, and loaded raw at `/chart` start, see MED-002) plants a git hook or a Claude Code hook that runs in every later session, with the session's credentials.
**PoC (reproduced):**
```
$ chart-unblock-probe.sh --ticket bd-9 -- git config core.hooksPath /tmp/evil-hooks
probe-exit: 0            # helper exit 0
$ git config --get core.hooksPath          # in the MAIN repo
/tmp/evil-hooks
$ HOME=$W/home chart-unblock-probe.sh --ticket bd-9 -- sh -c 'mkdir -p $HOME/.claude && echo "{...}" > $HOME/.claude/settings.json'
probe-exit: 0            # helper exit 0; $HOME/.claude/settings.json written
$ FAKE_TOKEN=secret chart-unblock-probe.sh --ticket bd-9 -- sh -c 'echo token=$FAKE_TOKEN'
token=secret             # the probe sees the session's secrets
```
**Fix:** Run the probe under a scrubbed environment (`env -i PATH=... HOME=<scratch> TMPDIR=<scratch> GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`), in a `git clone --shared` (or a worktree with `core.hooksPath` pinned to an empty directory and `extensions.worktreeConfig` on) rather than a worktree that shares `.git/config`; snapshot and compare hashes of `.git/config`, `.git/hooks/`, `.git/info/`, refs and `HEAD` as well as the working tree; require the skill to print the exact argv and confirm with AskUserQuestion before each run; correct SKILL.md:119-120 to name what the check cannot see.
**Reference:** CWE-78 https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html; CWE-250 https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/250.html; CWE-668 https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/668.html

### [HIGH-002] The research scope check is defeatable: its baseline marker lives inside the zone the subagent may write

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high) — confirmed by cross-model review (DISS-C-001)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:437` (marker path), `:447-448`, `:458-461`; `head/.claude/agents/chart-researcher.md:5`; `head/.claude/data/agent-types.yaml:27-28`
**Issue:** `marker()` writes the dispatch snapshot to `grimoires/loa/research/.chart-<slug>-<ticket>.dispatch` (`:437`), and `research-end` whitelists every path under `grimoires/loa/research/` (`:458`) and uses the same marker's mtime as the `find -newer` baseline for `.run/` and `.beads/` (`:461`). The chart-researcher agent has `Write` with no path restriction (`chart-researcher.md:5`, "Write exactly one file" is prose at `:24`) and `WebFetch` for arbitrary web content. The subagent can therefore Read its own marker, Write it back with the status lines of whatever it created elsewhere, and reset the mtime baseline in the same move.
**Impact:** A prompt-injected researcher writes anywhere in the repository (`.claude/hooks/*`, `.claude/settings*.json`, `grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml`, another ticket's report) and the ticket still closes clean; the poisoned report is later inlined into the priority-1 "settled decisions" snapshot (`:366`, `:382-390`).
**PoC (reproduced):**
```
$ chart-ticket.sh research-begin --map m --ticket t --root $F
$ echo evil > $F/.claude/hooks/planted.sh            # out-of-zone write
$ chart-ticket.sh research-end --map m --ticket t --root $F ; echo $?
1                                                    # honest marker: caught
$ git -C $F status --porcelain --untracked-files=all --ignored=matching \
    > $F/grimoires/loa/research/.chart-m-t.dispatch  # the subagent rewrites its marker
$ chart-ticket.sh research-end --map m --ticket t --root $F ; echo $?
0                                                    # planted.sh is still there
```
**Fix:** Remove `Write` from the researcher's tools (return the report as the final message; the session saves it) and set `write_capable: false` in agent-types.yaml. If a Write path is kept: store the marker outside the writable zone (`.run/` or a `mktemp` directory whose path is held by the session, mode 0444), and compare content hashes of the tree rather than status lines.
**Reference:** CWE-807 https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/807.html; CWE-284 https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/284.html; OWASP LLM01 https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm01-prompt-injection/

### [HIGH-003] `research-end` fails every honest run: the harness's own Write hook trips the `.run/` sweep

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:459-466`
**Issue:** Any file under `.run/` or `.beads/` newer than the marker fails the ticket (`:461-466`). The framework's PostToolUse hook for `Write` (`.claude/settings.json` matcher `Write` → `.claude/hooks/audit/write-mutation-logger.sh`, which appends to `.run/audit.jsonl` at its `:86`, `:93`) fires on the researcher's report Write, so the sanctioned flow (SKILL.md:143-149) can never close a research ticket. Any `br` call during the "claim all, begin all, dispatch all, end all" batch touches `.beads/` the same way.
**Impact:** A security check that always fails is a check operators disable. Combined with HIGH-002 the fence is both bypassable by an attacker and impassable for an honest run.
**PoC (reproduced):**
```
$ chart-ticket.sh research-begin --map m --ticket t --root $F; sleep 1
$ echo '{"hook":"write-mutation-logger"}' >> $F/.run/audit.jsonl     # what the Write hook does
$ printf '> UNTRUSTED research output: ...\n' > $F/grimoires/loa/research/chart-m-t.md
$ chart-ticket.sh research-end --map m --ticket t --root $F
chart-ticket: FAIL: the research subagent changed files outside grimoires/loa/research/; the ticket fails:
?? .run/audit.jsonl
```
**Fix:** Take `Write` away from the researcher (HIGH-002) so the session's own Write is the only one and happens after `research-end`'s baseline no longer matters; otherwise exempt the harness's append-only logs by name and compare `.beads/` content hashes, and add a test that fires the Write hook between begin and end.
**Reference:** CWE-754 https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html

### [HIGH-004] The FR-1.1 spike carve-out fails open on jq 1.6: an unparsable ledger allows `git branch -D spike/<slug>`

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:651-656` (function `_fr11_spike_decided` `:642`; call site `:691`)
**Issue:** `yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$ledger" 2>/dev/null | jq -e ... >/dev/null 2>&1` (`:651`) returns jq's status, and the hook has no `pipefail`. On jq 1.6 (Debian/Ubuntu default, the version on this host) `jq -e` exits 0 on empty input, so a yq parse failure makes `_fr11_spike_decided` succeed, `_fr11_all_merged` `continue`s at `:691`, and the force-delete is allowed. The header's own promise, "any failed lookup keeps the block" (`:638`), does not hold. The PR's test `D-5.9: an unparsable ledger keeps the block` (`head/tests/unit/spike-validator.bats:262-268`) fails on this host.
**PoC (reproduced):**
```
$ printf '' | jq -e 'any(.[]; .)' ; echo $?       # jq-1.6
0
$ printf 'decisions: [unclosed\n' > grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml
$ echo '{"tool_input":{"command":"git branch -D spike/ceiling-ui"}}' | block-destructive-bash.sh ; echo $?
0                                                 # unmerged spike commit: allowed
$ rm grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml ; <same> ; echo $?
2   BLOCKED [FR-1.1]
```
**Fix:** `j=$(yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$ledger" 2>/dev/null) || return 1; [[ -n "$j" ]] || return 1; printf '%s' "$j" | jq -e ... || return 1` (any non-zero jq status is "not decided"); run `spike-validator.bats` on jq 1.6 in CI.
**Reference:** CWE-636 https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/636.html; CWE-754 https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html

### [HIGH-005] SP-1 lets spike content land on another branch through shapes it never inspects, including the exact push the skill is allowlisted for

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:867-897` (rules), `:830` (Allowed), `:834-836` (Misses), `:854` (create flags pass); `head/.claude/skills/charting-decisions/SKILL.md:5` (`Bash(git push -u origin spike/*)`)
**Issue:** The rule D-5.4 implements is "spike content never enters another branch". SP-1 inspects `merge|rebase|pull|cherry-pick`, `checkout <ref> [--] <path>`, `restore --source` and `gh pr create`. It never looks at a push refspec, at branch creation from a spike ref, or at ref plumbing. Every shape below exits 0 from the head hook (reproduced); none is in the Misses comment at `:834-836`:
```
git push origin spike/ceiling-ui:main
git push -u origin spike/ceiling-ui:main          # matches the skill's own allowlist prefix (SKILL.md:5)
git push origin +spike/ceiling-ui:refs/heads/feat
git checkout -B main spike/ceiling-ui             # resets main to the spike; :854 passes every create flag
git checkout -b feat spike/ceiling-ui
git branch feat spike/ceiling-ui
git fetch origin spike/ceiling-ui:feat
git reset --soft spike/ceiling-ui
git update-ref refs/heads/main spike/ceiling-ui
git read-tree -u -m spike/ceiling-ui
```
`git merge spike/ceiling-ui` and `git checkout spike/ceiling-ui -- src/x` are blocked as declared.
**Impact:** The planning skill, whose only git write grants are `git worktree add *` and `git push -u origin spike/*`, can publish spike content directly onto `main` with one allowlisted command, and an operator reading the Allowed/Misses comments believes the invariant holds.
**Fix:** Block `git push` whose refspec source matches `_sp1_ref` and names a destination (`spike/x:<dst>`, with or without `+`); block `checkout -B|-b <new> <spike ref>`, `branch <new> <spike ref>`, `fetch <remote> <spike ref>:<local>`, `reset [--soft|--mixed|--hard] <spike ref>`, `update-ref ... <spike ref>`, `read-tree <spike ref>`; narrow SKILL.md:5 to `Bash(git push -u origin spike/*)` only after the hook rejects refspecs; add corpus rows for each; list whatever remains in the Misses comment.
**Reference:** CWE-693 https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/693.html

### [HIGH-006] Unattended `close --consumed-by` retires a live map with no state precondition; CD-22 asserts the defect

Any `br` call during the "claim all, begin all, dispatch all, end all" batch touches `.beads/` the same way.
**Impact:** A security check that always fails is a check operators disable. Combined with HIGH-002 the fence is both bypassable by an attacker and impassable for an honest run.
**PoC (reproduced):**
```
$ chart-ticket.sh research-begin --map m --ticket t --root $F; sleep 1
$ echo '{"hook":"write-mutation-logger"}' >> $F/.run/audit.jsonl     # what the Write hook does
$ printf '> UNTRUSTED research output: ...\n' > $F/grimoires/loa/research/chart-m-t.md
$ chart-ticket.sh research-end --map m --ticket t --root $F
chart-ticket: FAIL: the research subagent changed files outside grimoires/loa/research/; the ticket fails:
?? .run/audit.jsonl
```
**Fix:** Take `Write` away from the researcher (HIGH-002) so the session's own Write is the only one and happens after `research-end`'s baseline no longer matters; otherwise exempt the harness's append-only logs by name and compare `.beads/` content hashes, and add a test that fires the Write hook between begin and end.
**Reference:** CWE-754 https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html

### [HIGH-004] The FR-1.1 spike carve-out fails open on jq 1.6: an unparsable ledger allows `git branch -D spike/<slug>`

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:651-656` (function `_fr11_spike_decided` `:642`; call site `:691`)
**Issue:** `yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$ledger" 2>/dev/null | jq -e ... >/dev/null 2>&1` (`:651`) returns jq's status, and the hook has no `pipefail`. On jq 1.6 (Debian/Ubuntu default, the version on this host) `jq -e` exits 0 on empty input, so a yq parse failure makes `_fr11_spike_decided` succeed, `_fr11_all_merged` `continue`s at `:691`, and the force-delete is allowed. The header's own promise, "any failed lookup keeps the block" (`:638`), does not hold. The PR's test `D-5.9: an unparsable ledger keeps the block` (`head/tests/unit/spike-validator.bats:262-268`) fails on this host.
**PoC (reproduced):**
```
$ printf '' | jq -e 'any(.[]; .)' ; echo $?       # jq-1.6
0
$ printf 'decisions: [unclosed\n' > grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml
$ echo '{"tool_input":{"command":"git branch -D spike/ceiling-ui"}}' | block-destructive-bash.sh ; echo $?
0                                                 # unmerged spike commit: allowed
$ rm grimoires/loa/decisions.yaml ; <same> ; echo $?
2   BLOCKED [FR-1.1]
```
**Fix:** `j=$(yq -o=json -I0 '.' "$ledger" 2>/dev/null) || return 1; [[ -n "$j" ]] || return 1; printf '%s' "$j" | jq -e ... || return 1` (any non-zero jq status is "not decided"); run `spike-validator.bats` on jq 1.6 in CI.
**Reference:** CWE-636 https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/636.html; CWE-754 https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/754.html

### [HIGH-005] SP-1 lets spike content land on another branch through shapes it never inspects, including the exact push the skill is allowlisted for

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/.claude/hooks/safety/block-destructive-bash.sh:867-897` (rules), `:830` (Allowed), `:834-836` (Misses), `:854` (create flags pass); `head/.claude/skills/charting-decisions/SKILL.md:5` (`Bash(git push -u origin spike/*)`)
**Issue:** The rule D-5.4 implements is "spike content never enters another branch". SP-1 inspects `merge|rebase|pull|cherry-pick`, `checkout <ref> [--] <path>`, `restore --source` and `gh pr create`. It never looks at a push refspec, at branch creation from a spike ref, or at ref plumbing. Every shape below exits 0 from the head hook (reproduced); none is in the Misses comment at `:834-836`:
```
git push origin spike/ceiling-ui:main
git push -u origin spike/ceiling-ui:main          # matches the skill's own allowlist prefix (SKILL.md:5)
git push origin +spike/ceiling-ui:refs/heads/feat
git checkout -B main spike/ceiling-ui             # resets main to the spike; :854 passes every create flag
git checkout -b feat spike/ceiling-ui
git branch feat spike/ceiling-ui
git fetch origin spike/ceiling-ui:feat
git reset --soft spike/ceiling-ui
git update-ref refs/heads/main spike/ceiling-ui
git read-tree -u -m spike/ceiling-ui
```
`git merge spike/ceiling-ui` and `git checkout spike/ceiling-ui -- src/x` are blocked as declared.
**Impact:** The planning skill, whose only git write grants are `git worktree add *` and `git push -u origin spike/*`, can publish spike content directly onto `main` with one allowlisted command, and an operator reading the Allowed/Misses comments believes the invariant holds.
**Fix:** Block `git push` whose refspec source matches `_sp1_ref` and names a destination (`spike/x:<dst>`, with or without `+`); block `checkout -B|-b <new> <spike ref>`, `branch <new> <spike ref>`, `fetch <remote> <spike ref>:<local>`, `reset [--soft|--mixed|--hard] <spike ref>`, `update-ref ... <spike ref>`, `read-tree <spike ref>`; narrow SKILL.md:5 to `Bash(git push -u origin spike/*)` only after the hook rejects refspecs; add corpus rows for each; list whatever remains in the Misses comment.
**Reference:** CWE-693 https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/693.html

### [HIGH-006] Unattended `close --consumed-by` retires a live map with no state precondition; CD-22 asserts the defect

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high) — confirmed by cross-model review (DISS-C-002)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:402-404`, `:413-417`, `:420-423`, `:433`; `head/tests/unit/charting-decisions.bats:347-350`
**Issue:** The `--consumed-by` branch validates only the cycle-id shape (`:403`) and skips the context check that the `--reason` branch performs (`:407-408`). It then rejects every open row (`:414-417`), closes every bead and the epic (`:420-428`) and sets Status `closed` (`:433`), regardless of whether the map was ever handed off. The one unattended exception exists so `/plan-and-analyze` can retire a map it consumed (chart.md:82, plan-and-analyze.md hunk), which presupposes Status `handed-off` and zero open rows. CD-22 (`:347-350`) runs the command on a `charting` map with three open tickets and asserts success.
**Impact:** Any autonomous or prompt-injected session destroys the operator's in-progress chart with one allowlisted call: open decisions become `rejected` ledger rows and closed beads.
**Fix:** In the `--consumed-by` branch `die` unless `doc_field Status` is `handed-off` and the open-row count is 0; make `closed`/`abandoned` a no-op re-run; rewrite CD-22 to hand off first and add the negative case; have `chart-guard.sh --close-consumed` perform the same check so both layers agree.
**Reference:** CWE-862 https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/862.html

### [HIGH-007] The interactive-only rule is prose: every `chart-ticket.sh` write subcommand runs unattended

**Severity:** HIGH (confidence: high)
**File:** `head/.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh:159` (`op_epic`), `:199` (`op_ticket`), `:242`, `:256`, `:291` (`op_resolve`), `:331` (`op_rule_out`), `:351` (`op_handoff`), `:438` (`op_research_begin`); `head/.claude/skills/charting-decisions/SKILL.md:5`, `:71-74`
**Issue:** Only `close --reason` consults `dec-write-lib.sh context` (`:407-408`). `chart-guard.sh` refuses correctly but is invoked only by the skill's Step 0 prose (SKILL.md:71), while the allowlist grants `Bash(.claude/scripts/chart-ticket.sh *)` directly (SKILL.md:5). `LOA_UNATTENDED=1 chart-ticket.sh epic ...` creates the epic and doc; `ticket` writes open ledger rows and beads (reproduced by the review, confirmed by reading the code paths: no `need_interactive` exists).
**Impact:** The feature's premise, "a map whose rounds the agent answered is not a map" (chart.md:79-82), has no mechanical fence at the write path. An autonomous run that drifts into `/chart` produces a map of its own answers and hands it off as "settled; confirm, do not re-ask" context.
**Fix:** Add a `need_interactive` precondition (same fail-closed semantics as chart-guard.sh:41-54) to every write subcommand, exempting `--dry-run` and the repaired `close --consumed-by` path; one test per subcommand under `LOA_UNATTENDED=1`.
**Reference:** CWE-862 https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/862.html

Confirmed by cross-model review (DISS-C-007).

The hook therefore accepts a trust anchor authored by the actor it fences. From cross-model review (DISS-C-005).

The audit is complete. Verdict: **CHANGES_REQUIRED**, written to `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/auditor-sprint-feedback.md` with a consistent LOA-VERDICT trailer (verified by `verdict-derive.sh`). No COMPLETED marker was created.

**Tally:** 0 critical, 7 high, 8 medium, 9 low. Every high finding was reproduced against the head scripts in an isolated tree. The script is at `.eval/tmp/audit-repro.sh`.

**The seven highs**

- **Unblock probe sandbox is false.** Its only check is a git-status string compare. A probe set the main repo's `core.hooksPath`, wrote a file into HOME, and read a session secret, all with exit 0.
- **Research scope check is defeatable.** The dispatch marker sits inside `grimoires/loa/research/`, which the Write-capable researcher may write. Rewriting the marker hid an out-of-zone write and the ticket closed clean. The dissent's companion voice found this independently.
- **Research scope check also fails every honest run.** The framework's own Write hook appends to `.run/audit.jsonl`, which the sweep treats as a violation.
- **FR-1.1 spike carve-out fails open on jq 1.6.** An unparsable ledger lets `git branch -D spike/x` through. The PR's own test for this fails on this host.
- **SP-1 misses the shapes that matter.** Refspec pushes (`spike/x:main`, including the `-u` form the skill is allowlisted for), `checkout -B main spike/x`, `branch new spike/x`, `fetch`, `reset --soft`, `update-ref`, and `read-tree` all pass. None is in the documented Misses.
- **Unattended `close --consumed-by` destroys a charting map.** No Status or open-row precondition. Test CD-22 asserts the defect.
- **Interactive-only rule is prose.** No `chart-ticket.sh` write subcommand checks the context, while the allowlist grants the script directly.

**Mediums** cover awk `-v` escape injection into the map doc, raw loading of untrusted research reports as command context, orphan epics on doc-write failure, missing answer refs at hand-off, the agent-editable ledger as the FR-1.1 trust anchor, status-line blindness to pre-dirty files, the missing CHANGELOG and CLAUDE.loa.md entries for two new safety rules, and the run-mode ICE refspec push onto master.

**Dissent.** The review's run had hit the 200c budget cap. I re-ran it with a 400c budget. Two independent voices succeeded with no rejected payloads, so this is not a degraded review. Both voices' findings are triaged in the report.

**Process notes.** The review verdict was CHANGES REQUIRED rather than "All good", so the normal audit prerequisite was not met. The task instructions directed the audit to proceed, and that is recorded in the report. Supporting artifacts: `a2a/audits/2026-10-19/findings.jsonl`, the recon working file beside it, a trajectory log, and an updated NOTES.md.

**Next step for the sprint:** fix the highs with their named regression tests, re-run `/review-sprint sprint-1` to approval, then `/audit-sprint sprint-1`.
